answer: At first payout, the holder links a registered falconry licence, its number and one signed flight record from a meet above a ripple-marked lake, the falcon wearing a ferrous ring stamped with the number. Two verifiers match the record against the falconry register within a week; a record or ring claimed twice closes both. A licence costs 3 million rupiah a year, so one holder pays once while a thousand fakes need a thousand licences, 3 billion.
